longDescription:
Thirteen reasoning-and-review skills that run in any chat, with or without tools.

- dia-skopos: restates the goal, discloses assumptions and lists the decisions you must make, then waits for your approval before work starts.
- dia-elenchus: Plato's elenchus. Asks what you mean by a key idea, one question at a time, and shows where your own premises contradict each other.
- dia-quaestio: Socratic questions one at a time, then options, a comparison by your criteria, a verdict and a brief.
- dia-reductio: holds a position against its own commitments, derives any contradiction line by line and says which way out it would take.
- dia-negative: internal critique that holds a claim to its own standard and shows where it falls short.
- dia-warrant: finds the unstated rule behind an argument's step (Toulmin), tests it with critical questions and says how far the conclusion can be relied on.
- dia-conjecture: tests a universal claim against cases, finds the condition it needs and says whether the decision built on it stands (Lakatos).
- dia-counterplan: builds the opposing plan from your plan's key assumptions and says which plan the evidence favours and what would decide.
- dia-emend: one review pass over an answer or draft that fixes only confirmed defects.
- dia-ratchet: repeated review rounds in which only external checks count as evidence.
- dia-adjudicate: rules on reports others wrote about a text, checking each point against sources, and says what no report raised.
- dia-regula: checks or writes text a model will follow (a skill file, a prompt, an agent file) against four rules.
- dia-techne: deepens a request the way a field's top practitioners would, with a check by something other than the model, and runs it.

Start a message with a skill's name, or with dia: dia alone shows a menu (dia-router), dia reductio starts a skill by name, and dia followed by a request picks the skill that fits. A request that starts with neither starts no skill.

The skills are instructions only and ship no code of their own; dia-techne uses the tools your session already has, sends nothing private out, and stops before steps it could not undo. Each skill replies in the language you write in.
capabilities: Confirm the goal, assumptions and open decisions before work starts
Run a Socratic definition dialogue (elenchus) one question at a time
Brainstorm by Socratic questions, then compare options and give a verdict
Test a claim by strict reductio ad absurdum
Critique a claim by its own standard (internal critique)
Test how well an argument's reasons support its conclusion (Toulmin, critical questions)
Test a universal claim by counterexamples and find the condition it needs (Lakatos)
Build the opposing plan from a plan's key assumptions and weigh the two (dialectical inquiry)
Review an answer or draft once and fix confirmed defects
Run review rounds in which only outside checks count, with a round cap
Rule on reports others wrote about a text, point by point against sources
Write or review text a model follows against four rules
Deepen a request by a field's best practice, then run it with an outside check
defaultPrompt: dia-reductio remote work always raises productivity
dia-negative our company is flat, so anyone can speak up freely
dia-quaestio I need a weekend side-project idea
